newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly lower, pork bellies lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly lower, pork bellies lower.

text.p: CME hog futures ended mostly lower on profit taking and long liquiation while bellies finished near day's lows on local pressure, traders said.

Nervous trade developed in October hog futures after initial pressure on reports that packers were planning to cut back on the pace of slaughter due to tight hog supplies and declining cutout margins. Support developed during the day as traders bullish the market noted that the only reason packers may cut kills is because there are not enough market ready hogs available. Cash hog indications were mostly steady for Monday, they said.

Expectations that there will be no deliveries posted against August on first notice day Monday added to October's strength. October is at a discount to cash and it will be very hard to put numbers together to make a delivery with market ready hog supplies tight, they said.

However, December and forward contracts slipped again late on local pressure. Most of the weakness was attributed to profit-taking and long liquidation ahead of the weekend, especially after October through February contracts posted new contract highs on Thursday, they added.

R.J. O'Brien bought December late before locals sold. Rand Financials were net sellers while Stone Traders spread long February/short December. E.D.&F. Man spread short October/long April early, pit sources said.
In hog options, R.J. O'Brien bought October 58 calls ahead of expiration, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures ranged mixed early but moved down to new day's lows late as selling by Refco and locals hit sell stops. Futures generally showed pressure following the weak tone to cash bellies. The peak in bacon demand has passed, traders said.
"Cash is weak even with smaller kills seen ahead," one trader said.
Expectations that cash will remain under seasonal pressure also offset the talk that packers are planning to cut back on their pace of hog slaughter, traders added.
Hog futures closed 0.025 higher to 0.600 lower with only October up at 59.225 cents. Pork bellies ended down 1.175 to 0.600 cent with February off most at 77.050 cents.
